key_insight: MECx uses a bond-informed surrogate model to efficiently search combinatorial alloy configuration space and find lower-energy ordered MPEA structures than direct DFT Monte Carlo within practical limits.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster discovery of experimentally relevant ordered alloy states that can tune local structure, thermodynamics, and mechanical properties in complex multicomponent alloys.
method: Train surrogate energy models on 100 DFT-labeled configurations stratified in bond-count space.
Use the surrogate to guide Monte Carlo exploration of BCC ternary, quaternary, and quinary alloys.
Validate candidate ordered states against direct DFT Monte Carlo and simulated neutron diffraction signatures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that MECx found ordered configurations with lower energies than direct DFT-based Monte Carlo, and that the models transferred to selected binary subsystems without retraining.
watch_item: Performance depends on the representativeness of the compact DFT training set, so poorly sampled bond-count regions may limit reliability.
paper_title: Bond-informed search for ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys
